claims.text: Low-concentration Au doping of Pt nanoparticles on Al2O3 shifts the Pt d-band center.
The Au-induced d-band-center shift optimizes adsorption energies of reactants and intermediates.
Optimized adsorption energies enhance catalytic activity relative to undoped Pt nanoparticles.
Optimized adsorption energies enhance catalytic selectivity relative to undoped Pt nanoparticles.
Au dopants alter the local electron density around nearby Pt atoms.
The Au-induced change in local Pt electron density shifts the Pt d-band center.
The shifted Pt d-band center changes the binding energies of reactants and intermediates.
The electronic modulation lowers catalytic activation barriers.
Lower activation barriers improve turnover frequency and selectivity.
The proposed catalytic effect depends critically on uniform incorporation of Au into the Pt nanoparticles.
XPS or UPS can be used to detect the relevant Pt d-band-center shift.
HAADF-STEM can verify uniform Au dopant distribution in the Pt nanoparticles.
Au-doped Pt catalysts are predicted to show a measurable Pt d-band-center shift relative to undoped Pt catalysts.
The predicted d-band-center shift will correlate with increased CO-oxidation turnover frequency.
The predicted d-band-center shift will correlate with altered CO-oxidation selectivity.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold under low- to moderate-temperature CO-oxidation conditions when Au concentration remains low enough to avoid segregation or separate Au clusters.
The controlled comparison holds particle size, catalyst loading, support properties, synthesis parameters, and reaction conditions constant while varying Au addition.
Absence of a measurable d-band-center shift, or absence of an association between that shift and improved activity or selectivity, is specified as falsifying the hypothesis.
